state:
**Goal `ldap`, Stage 10 (the feature proofs) is under way.** Stages 1 to 5 and 7 to 9 are done; Stage 4 lacks only a CA a program supplies, and Stage 6 lacks only wiring the schema into the readers. `Core\Ldap`, `Core\Ldap\Filter`, `Core\Ldap\Dn`, `Core\Ldap\Sid`, `Core\Ldap\Ad` and `Core\Ldap\Change` owe nothing.

**The `samba-ad` domain is seeded, and the root `[ldap.corp]` reaches it.** The `20-novis-seed` script in `tests/db/compose.yaml` writes `OU=Company` before Samba starts (its comment lists every user, group and password), so healthy means seeded. The root `nvs.toml`'s `[ldap.corp]` binds over LDAPS at `localhost:16636` as the read-only `CN=Reader,OU=Company,DC=example,DC=test`, with `base` and `tls_ca_file`. A proof program that opens it carries `// requires: samba-ad`. The `Core\Ldap::connect` examples 01 and 03 and its attack now run live, and their `.out` show seeded people. All 52 live `.nvst` cases and the Rust `ldap` and `samba` tests pass on the seeded domain.

**Every flag reader is a feature that owes every proof** (`data/proofs/policy.json` has no exclusion by kind). `Entry::accountFlags` and `Entry::groupType` are the only way to get a flag object, so the `AccountFlags` and `GroupType` proofs read seeded entries: `carla.diaz` has `mustChangePassword` and a computed `passwordExpired`, `dora.lind` is `disabled`, `ben.kohl` has `passwordNeverExpires`, `Newsletter` is a distribution group, and `Employees`/`Managers` are global security groups.

**Traps for a live proof.** A search returns entries in no fixed order, and GUIDs, SIDs and timestamps differ per boot, so an example sorts what it prints and never prints those. A catch variable or a `var` reused in one file with another type does not compile (E0406): name each `LogicError` catch `$refusal` and each `Throwable` catch `$error`. An instance member's `covers:` line in a `.nvst` case goes at the end of the `--FILE--` block.

next.title: the feature proofs, read from the seeded directory

items.text: **`Core\Ldap\Entry` owes nothing** (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`; `bun nv proofs --id 'Core\Ldap\Entry::toArray'` prints the paths). `toArray` is at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/search.rs:682`, and `groupType` and `accountType` are at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/value.rs:226`. Each example, attack and bench carries `// requires: samba-ad` and reads `OU=Company` through `[ldap.corp]`. `--bless` each example and read its `.out`.

**`Core\Ldap\Ad\AccountFlags` and `Core\Ldap\Ad\GroupType` owe nothing**, reading flags from the seeded users and groups (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/flags.rs:18`). Their tests are done. They owe the about page, the examples, the attack and the bench.
**`Core\Ldap\Entries` (`references`, `total`) and `Core\Ldap\Changes` (`cookie`)**, whose Rust `covers:` marker is missing too (`crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/ldap.rs:1`).

backlog: `Core\Ldap\Connection::setPassword`, `changePassword` and `compare` owe every proof. A write needs an account of its own that a proof creates and deletes, because `Reader` changes nothing (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`).
Stage 6: wire the schema into the readers (`docs/agent/goals/ldap.md`).
Stage 4: a CA a program supplies (`docs/agent/goals/ldap.md`).
A run against a Windows Server evaluation VM is the user's to do by hand.
